reports.title: Key information relating to the cash dividend to be paid by Golar LNG Limited (Ticker: GLNG)

desk.headline: Revenue down 32% to $83.7m, just below estimate, as FLNG Hilli leaves Cameroon; dividend held at $0.25; no guidance
results: Revenue fell 32% to $83.7m and adjusted EBITDA 33% to $55.8m, mainly because FLNG Hilli finished its Cameroon contract and sat between jobs.
Net income attributable to Golar was $22.6m, down 28%; nine-month profit is up 161% to $144.5m.
FLNG Gimi has shipped 50 cargoes and kept producing above its contracted rate.
Golar took the final investment decision on a fourth FLNG (3.5 MTPA, about $2.45bn budget) and reserved long-lead items for a fifth.
A $500m 7.5% bond and a larger Hilli lease financing lift available liquidity to about $2.27bn; the $0.25 dividend is unchanged.

guidance.summary: Golar gives no formal earnings guidance. It points to contract backlog instead: about $5.7bn of EBITDA for Hilli's 20-year Argentina deal and about $8bn for FLNG Esperanza.

points: Hilli's roughly $350m upgrade in Singapore is on time and on budget; arrival in Argentina is targeted for mid-2027.
Gimi has run about 12% above its base rate this year; management sees 10–15% over time and a stronger Q4.
Esperanza remains on schedule for completion late 2027, with start-up in 2028.
Talks on a roughly 20-year charter for FLNG 4 are advanced; FLNG 5 waits until FLNG 4 is contracted.
Management pointed to the buyback programme, and flagged competition with data-centre builds for compressors and engines.

watch: Hilli's upgrade staying on budget and its move to Argentina in 2027.
A charter for FLNG 4 and the planned Esperanza long-term financing.
